# Why Jǫrð is spelled that way — and what it costs to get it right

There is a version of this name the early internet had to settle for: *jord*. This is the file on how **Jǫrð** replaced it.

The stories of Jǫrð circulate within the Norse corpus, where the figure embodies earth, mother of thor.

## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Jǫrð
- **ASCII form:** jord
- **Meaning:** "Earth"
- **Domain of influence:** Earth, Mother of Thor
- **Pantheon:** Norse
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** ᛁᚬᚱᚦ
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 212 of 463

## The Name Before the Marks


Spoken, the name runs `/jord/` — 'JORD' — pronounce the restored form with attention to the preserved diacritics and length.

## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Jǫrð** lives at [/jord/](/jord/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/jord/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/jord/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/jord/patterns/).

Tier-1 is not a compliment; it is a measurement. This restoration keeps something the ASCII form provably loses, and the measurement is repeatable.

## Where the Name Stood First

Jǫrð is attested in the textual and iconographic record of the Norse tradition. The temple on the web is the newest of these addresses — the first one that fits in a pocket.

## The Archetype at Work

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) seats this temple in **7 industries**, each match argued and weighted: **Agriculture, Food & Harvest** (earth personified and mother of Þórr; the soil from which every harvest grows.); **Mythic Name Restoration** (old Norse earth, whose ǫ distinguishes it from modern Jörð.); **Diacritic-First Domains** (the Old Norse ǫ in Jǫrð distinguishes it from modern Jörð.). The [Resonance File](/jord/blog/resonance/) reads those seats through the myths themselves.

## In the Sacred Texts

The Norse tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Poetic Edda](/texts/poetic-edda/) and [Prose Edda](/texts/prose-edda/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.

## The Emblems

The name does not travel alone. **Restored Name** — The Unicode form Jǫrð carries the original marks of the Norse tradition.; **Source Script** — Preserved through scholarly transliteration and canonical sources.; **Domain** — Earth, Mother of Thor. Each emblem is filed in the temple's record with its own provenance, the same discipline the spelling gets.

## For the Voice

'JORD' — pronounce the restored form with attention to the preserved diacritics and length. The reconstructed line runs `/jord/` — the temple's pronunciation atlas carries the phonemes one by one.

## The Discipline It Answers To

This restoration belongs to Norse, a tradition that wrote its endings down in advance and sang them anyway. The rules that govern it are not house style; they are the tradition's own scholarship, applied with the same care here as in any edition — and published, with the sources, so the file can be checked the way an edition can be checked. Tier-1 is not a compliment; it is a measurement. This restoration keeps something the ASCII form provably loses, and the measurement is repeatable.
